units.title: Temperature Measurement Techniques
topics: 1.1. Introduction to Temperature Measurement  Heat and Temperature – definition  Temperature Scales: Celsius, Fahrenheit, and Kelvin (relationships and conversions)
1.2. Expansion Thermometers  Construction, working, merits and demerits of: o Solid expansion thermometer o Liquid expansion thermometer

1.3. Filled System Thermometers  Construction, working, applications, merits and demerits of: o Class I – Liquid filled systems o Class II – Vapour pressure systems o Class III – Gas filled systems o Class V – Mercury filled systems  Sources of error in filled system thermometry  Effects influencing filled system thermometers: o Ambient effect o Head effect o Radiation effect o Immersion effect o Dip effect

1.4. Thermocouples  Thermocouple Principles o Seebeck, Peltier and Thomson effects.  Thermoelectric Laws o Law of Homogeneous Materials o Law of Intermediate Metals o Law of Intermediate Temperatures  Cold Junction Compensation o Need for cold junction compensation and commonly used CJC methods.  Thermocouple Types & Extension Wires o Positive and negative extension wires used for thermocouple types B, E, J, K, R, S, T.  Selection Criteria o Factors considered for selecting a thermocouple for industrial applications.

1.5. Resistance Temperature Detectors (RTD)  Industrial RTD construction  Lead wire compensation – need and concept  Measuring circuits for RTD: o 2-wire o 3-wire o 4-wire

1.8. 1.9. Temperature Switches and Thermostats  Operation of temperature switches and thermostats  Calibration procedure for temperature measuring devices

units.title: Level Measurement Techniques

2.2. Classification of Level Measurement Methods
2.2.1. Direct Methods  Construction, working, applications, merits and demerits of: o Sight Glass / Gauge Glass
2.2.2. Indirect Methods
2.2.2.1. Hydrostatic Pressure Type  Construction, working, applications, merits and demerits of: o Pressure Gauge Type o Air Purge System

2.2.2.2. Electrical / Electronic Methods  Construction, working, applications, merits and demerits of: o Capacitance Level Detector o Radiometric (Radiation ) Level Detector o Ultrasonic Level Detector o Radar Level Detector (Non-contact radar & Guided wave radar) o Laser Level Sensor o Differential Pressure (DP) Type Level Measurement

2.3. Level switches  Construction and working of: o Float type level switch o Displacer type level switch o Conductivity level switch o Tuning fork level switch o Rotating paddle level switch o Microwave level switch
